questions.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 7,364,982?
questions.solution: The 7 is in the millions place, so its value is 7,000,000.

questions.q: Which number is the greatest?
questions.solution: Comparing hundred-thousands (9) then ten-thousands (8) then thousands (3 > 2): 4,983,100 is greatest.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly arranges the numbers 6,145,200, 6,154,200 and 6,145,020 in ascending order?
Round 3,847,562 to the nearest hundred thousand.
questions.solution: Ten-thousands digit is 4 (<5), so round down to 3,800,000.

questions.q: Round 6,995,430 to the nearest ten thousand.
questions.solution: Thousands digit is 5, so the ten-thousands digit 9 rounds up and carries into the millions place: 7,000,000.

A bakery bakes 18 trays of 24 muffins each. 45 muffins are sold. How many muffins are left?
A canteen has 15 trays of 24 buns each. 3 whole trays are found stale and thrown away. The rest are sold at $2 each. Which expression gives the total sales in dollars?
questions.solution: First find trays left (15−3), then buns, then dollars: (15−3)×24×2.

In a triangle, the height is always:
options: equal to one of the sides
the perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex
the longest side of the triangle
questions.solution: The height is the perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has legs of 6cm and 9cm, and a hypotenuse of about 10.8cm. Which pair of lengths can be used directly as base and height?
questions.solution: The two legs (6cm and 9cm) meet at the right angle, so they can be used directly as base and height.

A tank is 2/3 full of water. After 20 litres are removed, it becomes 1/3 full. Find the capacity of the tank.
questions.answer: 2/3 − 1/3 = 1/3 of tank = 20 l, so full capacity = 60 litres

questions.q: Peter and Mary each had the same number of storybooks at first. Peter gave away 1/3 of his storybooks and Mary gave away 1/2 of hers. Mary was then left with 54 fewer storybooks than Peter. How many storybooks did each of them have at first?
questions.answer: Let each start with u books. Peter left: 2/3u. Mary left: 1/2u. Difference: 2/3u − 1/2u = 1/6u = 54, so u = 324. Each had 324 storybooks at first (Peter then had 216, Mary then had 162).

questions.q: In triangle PQR, PQ is chosen as the base. Describe how you would find the height for this base, and state one property this height must have.
questions.answer: Draw a line from vertex R perpendicular to line PQ (extending PQ if necessary). This height must form a right angle (90°) with the base PQ.
